attempts.note: the generic REST API every DocType gets: list/create under /api/resource/{doctype}, read/update/delete under /api/resource/{doctype}/{name}, and the /api/method/<dotted.path> RPC convention

frappe.client, the framework's own whitelisted RPC module (get_list, get_count, get, get_value, set_value, insert, insert_many, save, rename_doc, submit, cancel, delete, bulk_update, has_permission, get_doc_permissions, get_password, attach_file, validate_link_and_fetch, ~20 methods total, all callable at /api/method/frappe.client.<name>). Read to confirm what the adaptor's getCount call (get_count) does server-side, and to check whether the other ~19 are reachable through the adaptor: they are not (see notes)

the third-party SDK the adaptor actually calls (frappeClient.db()...). Its FrappeDB class implements getDoc/getDocList/createDoc/updateDoc/deleteDoc/getCount (what the adaptor exposes) plus getLastDoc/renameDoc/getValue/setValue/getSingleValue/submit/cancel (which the adaptor does not expose as functions and so cannot reach)

notes: ERPNext runs on the Frappe Framework, whose generic REST API (documented once, applied to every DocType) is the source of truth here. Unlike most adaptors in this registry, @openfn/language-erpnext has no generic get/post/request builder: every one of its six public functions (create, read, update, deleteRecord, getList, getCount) delegates straight to a fixed method on the third-party frappe-js-sdk's FrappeDB class, confirmed by reading that SDK's source. That SDK itself exposes more methods (getLastDoc, renameDoc, getValue, setValue, getSingleValue, submit, cancel, all thin wrappers around frappe.client.* whitelisted RPC methods) but the adaptor never calls them, so they are not reachable through it and stay out of scope: coverage:full here means the complete set of six endpoints this adaptor can actually issue, not the whole Frappe REST surface. Cross-checking against the SDK source also fixed two real bugs in the old spec's getList: the query param is `limit`, not `limit_page_length` (the SDK sends `limit`; Frappe's REST layer treats them as aliases, but the adaptor only ever sends the former), and `or_filters`/`group_by`/`as_dict` were missing entirely. getCount's `filters` param and optional `debug` flag are now modelled from the SDK call too. Documents are schemaless per doctype (Frappe lets any app define arbitrary DocTypes with arbitrary fields); Customer/Item/SalesOrder are kept as representative reusable shapes for common ERPNext doctypes, not an exhaustive list. Server URL is a placeholder site host, since the adaptor is configured with an arbitrary per-tenant baseUrl.
